audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Polewise supremum normalization destroys Green-kernel symmetry; The gradient-norm potential is not smooth orbifold metric and depends on embedding; Incorrect mass normalization in the regularized Monge-Ampere equation
limitations: P01 — Polewise supremum normalization destroys Green-kernel symmetry — Counterevidence: The mean-zero kernel is symmetric. GPSS v1 equation (5.17), page 19, uses a global shift over both variables. Self-adjointness does not rescue a pole-dependent shift.

P02 — The gradient-norm potential is not smooth orbifold metric and depends on embedding — Counterevidence: Euclidean comparability remains valid. The local potential sqrt(|Z1|^2+|Z2|^2+2|Z3|^2) pulls back to |u|^2+|v|^2. The example is A1 and within the assumptions.

P03 — Incorrect mass normalization in the regularized Monge-Ampere equation — Counterevidence: The scalar V_epsilon/I_epsilon restores mass equality. The klt SNC assumptions give dominated convergence I_epsilon -> V, so the coefficient tends to one and the uniform Lp and smooth-away estimates persist.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.
The report retains counterevidence and unresolved questions. Publication does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific adjudication remains pending; author adoption has not been requested.

repair.content:
Uniform L1 and a positive volume lower bound imply a uniform bound for m_epsilon. Set Gtilde=K-M with M>=sup(m+1). The Lp estimate survives a bounded shift, the second-variable gradient is unchanged, and the weighted gradient bound improves. A common off-diagonal subsequence preserves symmetry.

Use potentials with genuinely smooth orbifold pullbacks; justify compatible gluing and resolution Lp determinant bounds near Z.

Set c_epsilon=V_epsilon/I_epsilon.
